#4423. Every Pokémon Gimmick, Ranked

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

Over the years, we have seen many different Pokémon gimmicks pop up. It seems like every generation of Pokémon needs to have its own gimmick to make it stand out from the others.

It has come to a point where many fans of the series are tired of seeing new gimmicks pop up, and they would rather Pokémon go back to its roots with simple turn-based battles.

Unfortunately, that is never going to be the case, so you must accept whatever gimmick is in each game. Some of these gimmicks aren’t bad, but other ones are rather questionable. Let’s compare each of these gimmicks and see how they stack up against each other.

After introducing Mega Evolutions to Pokémon, Game Freak needed something to top it. Unfortunately, the gimmick in the next games, Sun and Moon, ended up being what is considered the worst gimmick in the Pokémon series.

The gimmick in question is Z-Moves. Z-Moves allow your Pokémon to use a massively powerful move, provided they are holding the appropriate Z-Crystal. Many have said that requiring an item to use one all-powerful move is a bit lame.

These all-powerful moves are often viewed as the one-hit option, allowing you to clear battles easily without much strategy being involved. The gimmick often felt unbalanced, and the addition of annoying, unskippable cutscenes, made using the moves extremely annoying.

I am someone who absolutely loves the Paldea region. I think that it is a beautiful area, and the idea that battles are celebrated in massive arenas is actually really cool to me. However, this generation of Pokémon games has one of the worst gimmicks, and that is Dynamaxing.

Dynamaxing allows a Pokémon to grow massive, amplifying its power in the process, and giving it access to different moves. In theory, it sounds decent. However, it is a nightmare for competitive play, as it makes already extremely powerful Pokémon even more powerful instead of lifting up and helping weaker Pokémon.

In addition to this, the moves given to the Pokémon are not unique, as they become different moves based on the previous move’s type, so a flying-type move will always become the same move when Dynamaxed. There are even more issues with it, but it all boils down to the gimmick feeling like not much thought went into it, as it is rather unbalanced and makes battles a bit of a slog.

Our picks for the best Pokémon Champions teams that are sure to help you climb this season.

If you were around for the Ruby and Sapphire days of Pokémon, then you remember double battles. These changed the way that Pokémon battles were played, and then they were expanded on in a rather weird way when triple Battles and rotational Battles appeared in Pokémon Black and White.

These battle types have rarely appeared since their inception, and it is because they weren’t very popular at the time. Triple battles are simple, involving three Pokémon being on the field at once instead of two. This is a bit unnecessary, as double battles were already fine.

Additionally, rotational battles were annoying because you had the ability to rotate your Pokémon around whenever you wanted, making some moves completely obsolete. However, it did make things interesting because the mechanic of rotating your Pokémon was different from switching them in and out of battle.

Terastallization is a gimmick that has the fanbase rather mixed, as there are many who enjoy the mechanic, and then there are those who absolutely hate it. As far as things go, it is a rather middle-of-the-road gimmick that could have been better, but it isn’t that bad.

This gimmick, which was introduced in Pokémon Scarlet and Violet, allows you to crystalize your Pokémon, changing its typing in the process. Many enjoy the mechanic because it lets you change the Pokémon’s typing, making them more resistant to moves they were once weak against.

The argument against Terastallization is that it can be unbalanced in certain battle formats, but it is mostly a balanced mechanic that works well with the series. The other argument is that every Pokémon looks absolutely terrible when it Terastalizes, and to be honest, they aren’t wrong.

Whether they're unlikely or just silly, these are the Ridiculous Pokémon Mega Evolutions We Would Love To See.

As stated earlier in the article, double battles were introduced in Pokémon Ruby and Sapphire, and they have remained to this day. It is one of the few earlier gameplay gimmicks that people sometimes forget started as a gimmick because it was so beloved.

Never before had players thrown two Pokémon into battle at once, and it felt like a natural progression of the battle system, allowing players to have two Pokémon whose types complimented each other.

Plus, this generation introduced new moves that were meant to be used during double battles. This gimmick has not changed since its inception, and it is because it feels natural for the series. There is nothing that needs to be changed about it, which makes it one of the best Game Freak has added to the series.

Why is it that I always forget that Mega Evolution is something that started in Pokémon X and Y? I always think that it was the gimmick from Pokémon Black and White. Tangent aside, Mega Evolution has become the most popular gimmick that Game Freak has added to the games.

It is so popular that people have continuously asked for more and more Pokémon to receive Mega Evolutions because the transformations are not only cool, but they are meaningful.

When Mega Evolution happens, it can sometimes change a Pokémon’s type, it can change the Pokémon’s ability, and it boosts the Pokémon’s stats tremendously. This can change the tide of a battle, but it isn’t so powerful that it is the ultimate trump card. It doesn’t allow you to blow away the opposition, but rather gives you more of a fighting chance and can dramatically help in certain situations. To this day, there are still Mega Evolutions being created, and it has been the focus in some competitive games as well.

I've missed Pokemon's Mega Evolution mechanic, and it's going to be a huge draw for Pokemon Legends: Z-A players.

#4422. Arc Raiders' latest patch adds two of the most requested features, but kills Cred hoarding

The last major Arc Raiders update of the year has arrived, bringing several big new features to the game, but not without some bad news.

Embark has just rolled out patch 1.7.0 for Arc Raiders players everywhere. This is a significant patch for the extraction shooter for a number of reasons, not least of which because it kicks off a series of events under the Cold Snap banner, which introduces a new conditions to the game’s maps.

Dig deeper into the patch notes, however, and you’ll find even more to get excited about, including features players have been asking for since the game’s first public test.

To start with, today’s update finally adds an option toggle aiming down sights. This is especially relevant for PC players, most of whom play shooters with an ADS toggle, rather than hold. Another often requested feature has been the ability to reset the game’s skill tree.

This is now available for the cost of 2,000 Coins per skill point. It goes without saying that you’re going to need a whole lot of money to reset the entire thing, but it’s a useful option to have when you want to alter your path.

The next change is one that’s going to ruffle a lot of feathers. Arc Raiders now has a soft Cred cap of 800. This is now clearly shown on your Wallet screen, and the developer said the cap is necessary to prevent players from using their accumulated Cred to unlock new Raider Decks immediately after release.

The good news is that this won’t affect the Cred you may already have, but going forward, 800 is the most you can hold at any point. You’ll also notice that Shani has more stuff for you to buy with Cred, in case you want another way to spend what you have.

Patch 1.7.0 also brings a few other additions - and makes some changes - that are worth highlighting. You can now customise your Raider Tool, which likely means we’re going to see Raider Tool cosmetics going forward.

Speaking of items, the Aphelion weapon blueprint has been moved to Stella Montis, so you won’t be able to get it from taking down the Matriarch. The Bettina, and Rattler have both seen some balance changes.

The Bettina’s durability will now degrade a lot slower per shot, making it take 26 magazines to fully deplete durability. The base magazine size has been increased to 22, and the reload time has been cut to 4.5 seconds. Embark says this should make the weapon more viable in PvP, while also allowing it to stand on its own without the need for players bring a secondary weapon.

As for the Rattler, the only change it gets is an increase to its magazine size from 10 to 12. The idea is to make it about as effective as a Stitcher or Kettle at close ranges when it comes to PvP encounters.

And, of course, it wouldn’t be a big Arc Raiders patch without some tweaks to the game’s Arc enemies. This time, the Shredder gets all the love. The menacing unit now moves faster, turns more sharply and doesn’t get knocked back as much when shot.

The Shredder’s head now has more health, too, meaning you won’t be able to shoot it off early and confuse it. In general, the Arc unit should be smarter, especially when navigating narrow spaces. Finally, the Shredder now activates faster upon detecting (and being attacked by) players.

Beyond that, the main menu has seen a few changes to highlight ongoing events, make certain announcements quieter, make it easier to track Raider Quests and more. There’s a lot more in this update, too, such as changes to footstep loudness, several tweaks to loot and the value of certain items, and more besides. You’ll find the full change log on the official website.

#4421. Elana Scherr: Chauffeur Life

My guests’ expertise in rear-seat amenities provides some insight into passenger-pleasing design.

From the November/December 2026 issue of Car and Driver.

The kids sure like to drink. Just not alcohol. Data shows that’s down by a considerable percentage among young people. Good for them. No, the youths in my social circle like to stay hydrated. They are never without a water bottle (bedazzled or stickered to set it apart from everyone else’s Owalas and Stanleys) or a sweet tea with a fat straw from a boba shop.

On a recent weekend visit from my college bestie and her teen and tween daughters, we must have hit every bubble-beverage and smoothie spot in town. All of that chauffeuring made me hyperaware of what makes for a well-appointed back seat. Number one, according to my expert passengers? Cupholders. Not just for drinks, but also for phones and sunglasses, because it’s easier to remember them when they’re sticking up rather than hiding inside a console or lying on a charging pad. Note to designers: Can you do phone-charging cupholders?

See all results for used cars for sale near 20016

The Ford Ranger that I had for the weekend got high marks for its back-seat cupholders and the fold-down console with its padded armrest. “I hate when there’s nowhere to lean,” declared the 16-year-old, weary already. It’s exhausting being so cool.

Complaints about the Ranger were the lack of dedicated climate vents for the back seat—their mother and I were freezing up front while they were still too warm in the back—and the hefty step-up into the cabin, which was challenging while carrying a large milk tea with mango jelly. “I can’t hold the door and jump down at the same time,” the younger one said, exhibiting a remarkable concern for parking-lot door dings rarely shown by people who don’t pay insurance premiums (and often not even by those who do).

A later ride in my ’80s Dodge Ramcharger had the same step-up and A/C problems, but the couchlike bench seat and full-length windows offset the lack of modern amenities. That vehicle is a favorite of my neighbor’s kids too, so if you’re investing in collector cars, grab a Ramcharger or a Plymouth Trail Duster before they go the way of vintage Broncos in price.

While trucks from that era might seem like a potential family travel solution, not everyone is willing to let their kids ride in a vehicle where the closest things to airbags are the Gabriel HiJackers someone installed in 1973 and the whoopee cushion that’s been under the seat since two owners ago. With that in mind, I made a list of some modern back-seat luxuries that have impressed me or my discerning young friends in recent new cars.

Dual Bluetooth connectivity: Unless you like being critiqued for your playlist, the ideal setup lets a back-seat passenger connect their phone for media while the driver links theirs for ­navigation­ and­ communication.­ I ­first ­noticed­ this ­feature ­on a Dodge Durango, but it’s increasingly common in newer infotainment systems.

See all results for used cars for sale near 20016

Third-row USB ports: It’s pretty much a given that second rows will have charging points, but with bigger families, that middle row is where the child safety seats latch in. While little ones might run low on apple juice, the older crew in the wayback will require a different kind of recharge. If you’re looking at base models, make sure to check the USB-port placement, as those are the trims most likely to cheap out on the third row.

Smart seats: I recently drove the new long-wheelbase Tesla Model Y L­ and­ noted that ­the­ middle-row­ chairs­ fold­ flat­ but­ don’t ­slide.­ While­ I wasn’t thrilled about having to make my way down the center aisle, airplane style, to get to the third row, I was impressed that the seatbacks in the second and third rows can be raised or lowered from the driver’s seat. Another neat trick is that if the front passenger’s seat is left too far back, it can adjust itself to prevent the middle row from crashing into it during folding. Also, the middle-row armrests automatically lowered when the door opened to make entry to the back easier. This is what I want from technology: smart seats. Now give me back a physical shifter.

Sparkle: At the end of the weekend, I asked the 11-year-old her thoughts on the Ranger. “It’s okay,” she said. “Only I like those cars where the tables fold out of the seats and the ceiling is all sparkly, like those caves where there are stars in the cave.” Rolls-Royces? I also like those cars. I respect her outlook, so I didn’t tell her what those cave stars actually are. Note to designers: Have you considered glowworms?

Like a sleeper agent activated late in the game, Elana Scherr didn’t know her calling at a young age. Like many girls, she planned to be a vet-astronaut-artist, and came closest to that last one by attending UCLA art school. She painted images of cars, but did not own one. Elana reluctantly got a driver’s license at age 21 and discovered that she not only loved cars and wanted to drive them, but that other people loved cars and wanted to read about them, which meant somebody had to write about them. Since receiving activation codes, Elana has written for numerous car magazines and websites, covering classics, car culture, technology, motorsports, and new-car reviews. In 2020, she received a Best Feature award from the Motor Press Guild for the C/D story "A Drive through Classic Americana in a Polestar 2."  In 2023, her Car and Driver feature story "In Washington, D.C.'s Secret Carpool Cabal, It's a Daily Slug Fest" was awarded 1st place in the 16th Annual National Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards by the Los Angeles Press Club.

#4419. It’s official: Battlefield 6 is 2025's best-selling game, but Black Ops 7 still managed to be November’s top-seller

2025 will be remembered for many things, but in the ultra-competitive games industry, it’s going to be thought of as the year Battlefield 6 did what many thought couldn’t happen.

Circan’s November 2025 video game sales report has easily been one of the most anticipated. For one, November is always one of the most lucrative for the games industry, but this year in particular has seen several major hits - including new entries in two rival series.

We’re talking, of course, about Battlefield 6, and Black Ops 7 the latest releases in their respective multiplayer shooter series. The decades-old fight to claim the top spot has long been won by Call of Duty, but the latest Battlefield has achieved what many thought was impossible.

Cricana’s report covers spending on video game software, hardware, and accessories in the U.S. November 2025 saw spending fall by 4% compared to November 2024, bringing in a total of $5.9 billion.

Software technically saw growth during the month, but declines in hardware, and accessories were mainly responsible for the drop in overall spending. Black Ops 7 continued Call of Duty’s 18-Year Streak in topping sales in its launch month.

However, this year’s game did not also top the year-to-date charts, something the series has done consistently, and more than any other top-selling game each year - with rare exceptions. Battlefield 6 is firmly in the lead there, cementing its claim as 2025’s best-selling title. Black Ops 7, fittingly, occupies in the #7 spot there.

Separately from the best-selling game title fight, November has actually been one of the worst for the industry in terms of hardware sales. The report notes that the three major platform holders - Sony, Microsoft, and Nintendo have all seen their hardware sales decline.

Spending on hardware during November amounted to only $695 million, a massive 27% decline compared to November 2024. According to the report, that’s the worst dollar amount total for any November since 2005, when it comes to hardware specifically. All three current-gen consoles totaled 1.6 million units sold, which Circana also notes is the lowest for any November since 1995.

This all doesn’t bode especially well for the industry. November has always been a key holiday shopping month, but it’s clear the constantly rising console prices - and already high game prices - have had a big impact.

#4418. Land of Arielia beginner's guide - 6 tips to maximise your idle time

If your main menu is starting to look a tad too cluttered for you, fret not - our Land of Arielia beginner's guide can help you make sense of this fast-paced idle RPG.

Just started playing Land of Arielia and wondering what you should focus on first? With so many upgrades, companions, equipment pieces, and progression systems to unlock, it's easy to feel a little overwhelmed. I did too the first time I unlocked the events, since they basically overwhelm the screen (I mean, look at the image below). So, I decided that a Land of Arielia beginner's guide is in order.

Land of Arielia beginner's guide Since Land of Arielia is designed to be a fairly relaxed idle RPG, you can handle most of the fighting automatically. You can shift most of your focus to getting stronger by making upgrades while your character keeps farming.

Below, we'll go over the most important things to know when starting out, including how to increase your combat power and what to prioritise as you progress.

Oh, and don't forget to claim these Land of Arielia codes too for some extra resources, or have a look at our Land of Arielia tier list to get a proper idea of which class to pick.

One of the most important things you can do early in Land of Arielia is progress through the stages. Clearing more stages increases your idle rewards, including the experience and currency you earn over time. It also helps unlock additional features, so that's a bonus.

I suggest you try to push through stages whenever you can, and each time you make an upgrade (in case you get stuck). Eventually, you'll encounter enemies or bosses that are too difficult to defeat consistently. When that happens, don't worry. It's a normal part of progression in idle games.

What you can do when that happens is collect whatever rewards you have available and equip any gear you might've gathered (if it's better). You can also spend some currency on upgrading your skills and companions, and then try to challenge the stage again.

Equipment plays a major role in increasing your CP. As you progress, you'll obtain gear with different rarity levels and stats, which can be upgraded by spending your Tempered Spark.

Early on, your main priority should be replacing weaker equipment with stronger pieces. The good news is that your enhancements carry on between gear swaps, so whatever you upgrade is a good upgrade. What should you do with unwanted/extra gear? Land of Arielia features a Smelting system that lets you convert unnecessary equipment into useful resources, such as Tempered Spark (which lets you further upgrade your gear).

Smelting can also contribute to upgrading your Smelting skill, which provides additional stat bonuses.

Instead of keeping every piece of low-level equipment in your inventory, make sure you regularly check which items are no longer useful and smelt them. Then, spend that resource upgrading your existing gear.

You can smelt the gear by going to the Craft menu and then to the Smelting tab.

Your character's abilities are another important source of damage and CP. You can upgrade the skills from the Skill menu on the bottom side of the screen, and spend the Energy Core to make the upgrades.

You can see the next level effect for each skill, so that can help you decide between them when making the upgrades manually. Alternatively, you can opt for the Quick Upgrade and simply go with levelling each one alternatively.

It's an easy progression system to overlook when you're busy trying to keep up with everything, but regardless, it shouldn't be overlooked.

Land of Arielia features several companion-related progression systems that can help improve your character. There are mounts, Spirits, and Dragonborn, and I won't even get into the other features such as Miragear, Mirasuit, Spirit Guardian and Back Accessory. All these work in a similar manner, except that some of them affect your character directly, while the others affect your... well, companions.

Mounts are useful overall, but they can also provide additional combat-related benefits through upgrades. Depending on the rarity and type, they can provide different stats (more offensive or defensive stats). You can also unlock mount-specific skills, so if you have the means, pick based on that.

Dragonborn companions offer another way to improve your stats and combat performance. They have their own upgrade and breakthrough systems, allowing you to upgrade them over time. The Dragonborn fights alongside you, so you want to have one that can do lots of damage and provide useful stats too.

The Spirit is like a pet that follows you around. It also provides bonus stats, and it has its own skills, so make sure you check them out and pick the one you like most. Many of the Spirits can be acquired via in-game events too, so that's a nice bonus.

I know this is going to be a big one, but Land of Arielia doesn't skimp when it comes to in-game events. There are at least a dozen of them, and they can all be found on the main screen. You should try to check them all regularly, and find a rotation that works for you.

By rotation, I mean completing them in a way that makes it easier for you personally. For instance, you can take them from top to bottom, or left ot right, or however you want. You can even do your dailies and leave the events for the grand finale.

Dungeons provide very useful progression materials, and you have limited attempts every single day. You should try to manage your time accordingly, so that you can complete all of them daily. The daily dungeons also come in different types: solo and multiplayer.

For the solo dungeons, you absolutely have to complete them. There are no ifs, ands, or buts, so that's something you need to add to your to-do list if you plan on playing the long-term game.

As for the multiplayer dungeons, they can give much better rewards, but they also require more players. You will have to queue up with some random players, but if you want to, you can also add friends in-game and plan daily dungeon runs with them.

#4417. Would You Rather: Cadillac Escalade IQ vs. Escalade-V

For about $160,000, are you taking the 682-hp supercharged gas Escalade or the 750-hp electric one?

A lot of companies build EV models that have an internal-combustion analogue, with the guiding principle of, “the car you liked before, but electric.” There’s a tight thematic cohesiveness to that approach—a BMW i3 and M340i each endeavor to arrive at their optimized level of BMW 3-ness despite the differing powertrains—but the Cadillac Escalade is not like that. Yes, there are gas and electric versions, but they’re similar only inasmuch as they each avidly pursue the high-level Escalade goals of cosseting bigness and cocky braggadocio. When Tony Soprano got an Escalade in season 5 of The Sopranos, the only question around that casting decision was, what took so long? Today Tony would have more choices in his pursuit of the maximum expression of GM SUV, as do any of us with about $160,000 to spend. Namely, would you rather have a supercharged V-8 Escalade-V or an electric Escalade IQ?

Cadillac designed the Escalade-V’s exhaust to be extra boisterous, adding a 360-degree loop to the passenger’s-side pipe to equalize the length with the driver’s-side counterpart, for maximum sonic awesomeness. The IQ does not have equal-length dual exhaust. Whatever exhaust it does produce will get you into a tedious and possibly confrontational discussion of well-to-wheel emissions with your uncle at Thanksgiving. However, you’ll never have to worry about thieves stealing your catalytic converters, so I’ll call that one a draw.

Hold on, that doesn’t sound right—let me check my notes—sorry, my curb-weight figure for the Escalade-V inadvertently included a Toyota GR86 parked on its roof. Remove that extra car, and the supercharged Escalade is quite a bit lighter: 6290 pounds for the V, and a pavement-crushing 9120 pounds for the IQ.

Despite the weight disparity, the two Slades are evenly matched in a drag race, with the 750-hp IQ trailing the 682-hp V by a couple tenths of a second to 60 mph (4.5 seconds to 4.3). On a rolling start from 5 mph, they’re tied at 4.7 seconds, and passing a dawdler will be a quicker task in the IQ: 50 to 70 mph in 2.6 seconds, versus 3.1 seconds for the loud Caddy.

Now, I’m old enough to remember the days when a Ferrari 458 Italia felt like it had pretty decent passing power, but the Escalade IQ’s 2.1-second 30-to-50-mph time beats the Ferrari by a tenth. If the IQ had been part of our Chariots of the Gods comparison test in 2011, its 50-to-70-mph time would have slotted it a tenth of a second behind the 458 and two-tenths ahead of the McLaren MP4-12C. Neither of those, when accelerating, heave their hoods skyward like a 70-foot Viking sportfish climbing on a plane, but the Escalade IQ certainly does. And they say EVs don’t bring any drama to the experience—behind the wheel, the IQ accelerating like my favorite Ferrari of all time feels as improbable as it actually is, like the vehicle itself is struggling to cope with its superpowers. An Escalade-V drives more like a mutant CT5-V Blackwing, and it’s definitely the Escalade where the driver’s seat is more desirable than one of the chauffeur chairs in back.

See all results for used cars for sale near 20906

If we accept that one of the primary goals for an Escalade is to project brash confidence, and that hugeness is fundamental to that project, the Escalade IQ wins going away. It reminds me of a scaled-up Rolls-Royce Cullinan in the side profile, and there’s a lot of side to behold: the IQ is more than a foot longer than the gas-powered Escalade. It’s also just newer, and I think it helps the premium aura not to have a bunch of Chevys and GMCs out there copping your style with very similar bodies. Also: rear-axle steering is unequivocally a flex, and the internal-combustion Escalade doesn’t have it.

Inside, both Escalades offer huge screens, lots of leather, and power-operated doors. However, only the IQ is eligible for the Curated by Cadillac program, wherein buyers fork over an additional $54,995 and get to choose from a huge palette of colors, inside and out. With 44 interior color choices, you can certainly spec a one-of-one IQ, while the Escalade-V sticks with “Yukon Denali, but fancier” as a guiding principle. Advantage, IQ.

When we’re discussing EVs versus internal combustion, range is usually an easy win for the gas-powered candidate. But not here—the Escalade-V has an EPA-rated 312 miles of range, while the IQ gets a 465-mile rating. Yes, the V will refuel a lot quicker, but you’ll be stopping way more often. And if your gas pump stops at $100, you might technically need to fill twice to top off the 24-gallon tank with premium.

Another factor I have to consider is rap music references, and on that front the Escalade-V is the easy winner, if only because the IQ is too new—most Escalade lyrics concern gas-powered models by default. Cadillac did hire Big Boi from Outkast to rap about the IQ, but that doesn’t count. (“Escalade IQ, this is the intro to, the all-electric Cadillac perfection ...”) I’m sure we’ll get there eventually: “Rolling in the IQ to the house with a view, IQ got the roof see-through, park the IQ next to the other ’cause I just bought two.”

Finally, I think part of the Escalade mystique has always hinged on leadership. This is a boss truck, from Sopranos to Succession. And where are the luxury winds blowing? It seems to me that in this space, which is to say “not a V-12 Ferrari,” the market is amenable to electrification and the technology is progressing fast. GM just announced that its forthcoming battery chemistry will improve range while being 20 percent more compact. There will come a time, maybe not far off, when EVs just make more sense objectively (they already do, depending on use case) and internal combustion will be the nostalgia play. So in this Would You Rather, I’m embracing that future and going for the Escalade IQ. The V is charming, but for $160,000, the IQ better fulfills the role of flagship SUV—quick, cocky, luxurious, and incontrovertibly baller.

Ezra Dyer is a Car and Driver senior editor and columnist. He's now based in North Carolina but still remembers how to turn right. He owns a 2009 GEM e4 and once drove 206 mph. Those facts are mutually exclusive.

#4414. This Grand Touring Coupe Is a Subaru Like No Other

It’s a 1993 SVX, and it’s for sale on Bring a Trailer.

Let’s face it, Subaru just isn’t weird anymore. A thoroughly mainstream company, it has enjoyed great success selling all-wheel-drive crossovers with lots of plastic body cladding to people who wear outdoorsy clothes while spending most of their time indoors. Subarus are safe. They are reliable. They are no quirkier than having extra pockets on your Gore-Tex pants.

However, once upon a time, Subaru was goofier than Mickey Mouse’s best pal. See an example of this delightfully odd past on Bring a Trailer (which, like Car and Driver, is part of Hearst Autos): a 1992 Subaru SVX in bright red, complete with low mileage, weirdo side windows, and flat-six power.

See all results for used 1993 Subaru SVX for sale near 33771

On paper, the SVX is a bit of a head scratcher. The design is Italian, done by Giugiaro’s Itadesign, and incorporates swelling curves and a glassy cockpit. The curb weight is considerable, at over 3600 pounds, and the 3.3-liter flat-six engine is unstressed at 230 horsepower. The only transmission offered was a four-speed automatic.

So, this was not some rally-crazed, boosted-to-heck Impreza sedan like a WRX, but a grand tourer. Parked next to various toaster-shaped Foresters in Subaru showrooms of the time, the SVX looked wildly out of place, especially with those inset power side windows.

The strangeness just added character. Further, the SVX proved nearly unparalleled at dispatching miles, no matter the weather conditions. Everything fans like about boxier, more utilitarian regular Subarus was present in terms of unflappable performance in terrible weather conditions. The SVX just added a level of leather-lined polish for a car that turned any sort of driving into effortless swanning.

This example is a limited-run 25th Anniversary edition and has just 16,000 miles on the odometer. Inside are niceties like a power driver’s seat, cruise control, automatic climate control, and a CD player that is hidden behind a faux wood panel. It’s a well-optioned car and would have cost the equivalent of $52,000 when new, adjusted for inflation.

Not all that popular in its day, an SVX makes for an interesting modern collectible today. It’s relaxing to drive, interesting to look at, and you don’t often see them on the road. Should Subaru bring back a modern version? Probably not, but the SVX does give a glimpse at a bygone time when Subaru was both weird and good.

#4409. Land of Arielia tier list (November 2026) - Thunder Gunner or Blaze Swordsman?

The best class will always depend on your preferred playstyle, but with our Land of Arielia tier list, we can help you make the most of your chosen build.

As soon as you set foot inside Land of Arielia, the first and most important decision you have to make is picking your class. There are four classes, and each one has its own benefits. This Land of Arielia tier list is meant to help you pick the one that fits your playstyle best, so let's dive right in. How important is your class? Picking your class is important from a couple of points of view: how you play and the way you tackle multiplayer dungeons. You typically want to deal as much damage as possible, so most classes are designed with that in mind. The main difference between them is the type of weapon they use, and whether or not they are ranged or melee.

At the moment, only the Swordsman has melee attacks, while the other three classes are ranged.  Is there a best class? Objectively speaking, there is a best class. This class has a lot of burst damage, which is great against bosses, but it also works great in PvE, clearing enemies with ease. The main reason one class is above the others is simply because of that, and nothing else.

For most casual players, the class they pick won't really matter. However, the playstyle and look of the character do, so there's that. I wouldn't worry too much if I were you, if you wanted to play something like a Frost Mage or an Archer. I personally have a Frost Mage, and it performs just right, except for the fact that Thunder Gunners can out-DPS you in dungeons if you don't have the gear upgraded.

Land of Arielia tier list The tier list matters mainly if you want to min-max everything, and if you want to play competitively. If you don't care much about having the most damage possible or you're more of a casual player, then take this with a grain of salt.

As a general rule of thumb, I would argue that the Thunder Gunner with the right gear and stats can out-DPS everything. You can check the rankings on your server (those can differ based on the server), but the fact that their kit relies heavily on explosions is a bonus.

Even though the Swordsman deals solid damage, they can also be a little bit tankier than the other classes, making them a class you'll often see in multiplayer dungeons.

I already mentioned that I play a Frost Mage, and personally, I feel like it's a solid pick. The main scaling is with ATK, and they rely on AoE.

Tempest Archers are also AoE-based, but their single-target skill is also solid. They are just like the Frost Mage, but with a slightly different kit. It's a fun class to pick if you prefer the physical damage approach instead of the magic one.

I suggest you check out the latest Land of Arielia codes so you can get some extra goodies to help your character grow too! Or if you're looking for more character rankings, our Don't Starve Together mobile character tier list and Legend of Witch tier list are a fantastic place to start.

#4407. Hungarian VW Bus Goes from ‘Matchbox: The Movie’ to Matchbox, the Toy Car

A 1976 Volkswagen T2 achieves fame and immortality.

Filmed in Budapest and Bratislava, Matchbox: The Movie has a fairly tenuous connection to the little die-cast toys. Starring the always charismatic John Cena as a CIA agent racing to deal with a rogue nuclear weapon, the central conceit is that a group of friends who used to play together with Matchbox cars in middle school reunite in adulthood to take down the bad guys.

It’s a movie that plays like a kid narrating a story while pushing die-cast cars around the carpet, which feels like a pretty good fit for the brand association. Compared to Hot Wheels, which are all about speed and pulling off loops on those iconic orange tracks, Matchbox as a brand skews a little more realistic, and often features construction machines and vintage vehicles.

See all results for used cars for sale near 78242

Speaking of iconic orange, one of the central vehicles onscreen is a 1970s Volkswagen T2, the beloved Microbus. These things are such a huge part of popular culture that one was the main plot point in an episode of Futurama, which saw the crew hopping into a VW Bus and following Beck’s band around. (Best joke: When asked by Professor Farnsworth where the onboard time dilation device is, Fry reaches under the seat and produces a bong.)

In this case, two VW T2s were used in filming, both owned by Budapest-based Dávid Sipos. One of the two needed sufficient modification for stunt driving that it ended up no longer road legal, but the more original of the pair survived the filming schedule unscathed and came back into Sipos’s possession. As a tie-in with the film, Mattel of course produced Matchbox models of the film cars, and Sipos was delighted to find that the blister-pack model of the VW Bus was a faithful match for his car, right down to the aftermarket sunroof and identical Hungarian license plate.

The story gets even better, with the involvement of the original owner who picked up the keys to this orange bus some 50 years ago. If a VW Microbus is a symbol of counterculture in the U.S., that’s not the case overseas. In 1964, reacting to European tariffs on U.S. chicken products, President Lyndon B. Johnson enacted the so-called “chicken tax,” slapping a 25 percent penalty on various products including imported European light trucks.

For Volkswagen, this meant the death knell of U.S.-exported T2 pickups and panel vans, so the Microbus was typically a passenger van stateside. In Europe, working T2s continued chugging along as part of the furniture of a busy city, getting people and goods where they needed to go.

See all results for used cars for sale near 78242

This particular 1976 T2B was delivered by train to Budapest for the Hungarian Water Works to use as a service vehicle. A young employee with the last name Thaly drove it right off the rail car at the depot, and it entered fleet service for the next eight years.

By 1984, something more modern was needed, so the company offered the VW to Thaly, who promptly snapped it up. He kept working, but the T2 effectively enjoyed a sunny retirement, stored carefully in a garage and used as a summertime camping vehicle driven throughout Europe, first with his children, then with his grandchildren. This went on for three decades.

In more recent times, Sipos was working for an advertising agency that often landed accounts for youth-oriented brands. “Somehow I was always the one suggesting that we should have a VW Bus covered in the brand’s graphics as part of the campaign,” he says.

The company eventually bought a slightly earlier 1972 T2A for permanent use as a rolling billboard. Far from just being a work vehicle, employees started borrowing it outside work and just driving it around, as the experience was so much fun.

“There’s something about traveling in a VW Bus that instantly creates a sense of community,” Sipos says.

The T2 became something of a signature of the agency, with friends and colleagues often flagging likely-looking vehicles up for sale. One day in 2013, Thaly’s beloved orange VW cropped up in a listing, and while the advertising company didn’t need it in the fleet, Sipos bought it as a personal vehicle.

This T2 ended up onscreen when Matchbox's director, Sam Hargrave, spotted a photo of it. Sipos also had a second, very similar T2 at the time, green in color, and it was the latter that was cloned to look like the 1976 T2B and modified for stunt work.

The story of how the actual Hungarian registration ended up on the toy car is a bit of a mystery, as the onscreen cars used different license plates. Mattel’s designers would have had piles of reference photos to comb through, and somehow it was settled that the detail on the plate would be DJN-623, the plate this van has been wearing since 1993.

Sipos made sure to get this unexpectedly accurate model of the Thaly family’s beloved orange Volkswagen to them, and he keeps in close contact with them. How typical of a Volkswagen Bus to still be bringing people together, 50 years after it hit the road.

This car is proof that the old GM’s ideas weren’t all bad, as I find out when I take custody of one.

From the November/December 2026 issue of Car and Driver.

Back in 2007, I gave my father-in-law, Roger, a ride in a Dodge Viper test car. He loved it, and I offhandedly said, “If you like this, a Saturn Sky Red Line is 80 percent of the performance for 30 percent of the price.” That was the extent of my salesmanship, so I was surprised a month or so later to learn that he’d gone out and bought a new Sky Red Line—for less than $30,000.

I mean, people ask me for car-buying advice all the time. But the way it usually works is that someone asks my pick for an electric sedan, I tell them to drive a Lucid Air, and then they buy an F-350 Power Stroke. So Roger’s follow-through was both rewarding and unnerving, because now he owned a Sky, and I owned my opinion, which is dangerous. I once had a boss who asked me to name a car that was “overpowered but understated,” and I blurted three words that I came to regret: “Volkswagen Phaeton W-12.” I think soon thereafter the company handbook was amended to make Phaeton recommendations a fireable HR violation.

See all results for used cars for sale near 55082

Fortunately, Roger liked the Sky, the first new GM car he’d purchased since a 1982 Camaro Berlinetta that was so terrible that he swore he’d never buy another GM vehicle. He usually sticks to such decrees, but maybe Saturn got a pass because the brand wasn’t around when his Chevy was putting him on a first-name basis with the local tow-truck dispatchers. In any case, the only problem the Sky ever had pertained to the notorious GM ignition-switch recall, wherein pre-bankruptcy GM’s pathological commitment to cheapness led to ignition cylinders unfit for a Little Tikes Cozy Coupe and thus occasional random engine shutdowns. This happened to Roger once on a back road, but he was unbothered. “I just put it in neutral, restarted it, and kept driving,” he told me. “Didn’t even stop.” I guess the Camaro might have permanently recalibrated his expectations for build quality.

Eventually, Roger stopped driving, but he still liked the Sky, so it sat in his driveway long enough for the neighbors to plant hedges so they wouldn’t have to look at it. But where they saw a dented, pollen-crusted car with two flat tires, I saw a dented, pollen-crusted car with two flat tires and a 260-hp turbo four, a stick shift, rear-wheel drive, and a limited-slip differential. Roger said that if I could get it going, I could have it for the bargain price of “get it out of my driveway.”

So, one day, I arrived with a battery jump pack, an air compressor, and five gallons of fresh gas. The questionable tires held air, and the electrics powered up. I splashed in some fuel and turned the key. The Sky fired up like it had been parked an hour before, its digital odometer showing just 43,000 miles. I put it in neutral, let out the clutch, and it immediately stalled because it wasn’t actually in neutral. Turns out you can wiggle the Red Line shifter side to side quite a bit even when it’s in second gear.

See all results for used cars for sale near 55082

Other revelations mostly pertained to ran-when-parked status. The flat-spotted tires and various wheel-on-curb encounters gave the Sky the ride and directional stability of a grocery cart you pull out of the corral and immediately swap for a different one. The battery wouldn’t hold a charge, the interior smelled like a cologne called Old Must, and the A/C didn’t blow cold. But the scrappy Red Line ran like a champ, the turbo issuing a jaunty chirp on upshifts and all 260 horses feeling ready to gallop. It just needed a little deferred maintenance.

I bought some Pirelli P Zeros and got an alignment, since I’ve found that cars drive better with round tires all pointed in the same direction. I changed the oil and recharged the A/C. Next, I tackled the battery, which is mounted somewhere near Earth’s molten core. Accessing it requires removing the right front fender, and I got impatient and only mostly unbolted it, figuring I could bend the flexible composite panel enough to get the battery out. That’s how I tore a fender while replacing the battery, which is not a sequence of words I expected to write back when I told Roger that a Sky Red Line is a discount Viper.

But I stand by my assessment. The Sky was, and is, huge fun. It’s agile and powerful, low-slung and eager to carve a corner. It makes any drive feel like Bowser and Koopa Troopa should be trying to beat you to the finish line of Rainbow Road. The critiques that dogged the Sky when it was new—cheap interior, little storage space, poor visibility—seem less important now. Saturn ran out of time to perfect the Sky, but it’s perfect enough. Dents and all.

Ezra Dyer is a Car and Driver senior editor and columnist. He's now based in North Carolina but still remembers how to turn right. He owns a 2009 GEM e4 and once drove 206 mph. Those facts are mutually exclusive.

#4403. Legendary game creator Vince Zampella has passed away

Vince Zampella, co-creator of Call of Duty, and a veteran studio head responsible for some of the biggest franchises in the world, is gone.

Vince Zampella, known for co-creating the Call of Duty series, among many other roles, has died. Zampella, 55, died in a car crash in Los Angeles on Sunday. The fatal crash killed him, along with the occupant of his car.

According to NBC, Zampella’s Ferrari hit a concrete barrier after leaving a tunnel in the San Gabriel Mountains, north of Los Angeles. Zampella was unfortunately trapped in an ensuing car fire, and the passenger was ejected.

Vince Zampella is one of the industry’s most prolific creators. His storied career is long, and is responsible for some of the biggest shooter franchises in history. It started with Medal of Honor in the 90s, a game that changed WW2 shooters forever.

Zampella later co-founded the legendary Infinity Ward in 2002, the team that would go on to redefine multiplayer shooters forever. Infinity Ward is the studio responsible for the Call of Duty series, which remains one of the biggest games for publisher Activision, and the entire industry.

Zampella then left the studio he founded in 2010 following a major fallout with Activision. He, along with longtime collaborator, Jason West, went to rival publisher EA to form Respawn Entertainment.

Respawn went on to create the Titanfall series, and later Apex Legends. The studio is responsible for non-shooters, of course, like the third-person action game series Star Wars Jedi. Zampella was instrumental in making the game possible, having hired God of War 3 director Stig Asmussen to helm a team within Respawn out of a desire to diversify the studio’s output and prove he can do more than make shooters.

Zampella had only recently met with journalists and peers at The Game Awards, where Battlefield 6 was nominated for multiple awards. Battlefield 6 is the most successful game in series history, in part as a result of Zampella’s leadership. The legendary leader was given the reigns of the struggling multiplayer shooter franchise in 2021, with a goal of finding a viable future.

Zampella’s sudden death has shaken the industry, and many mourn his loss as the news started spreading.

“We are heartbroken by the loss of Vince Zampella, a creative leader whose work shaped generations of players and helped define what modern shooters and action games could be,” EA said in a statement.

“While his impact reached far beyond any one game or studio, we will remember Vince for how he showed up every day, trusting his teams, encouraging bold ideas, and believing in Battlefield and the people building it. We are deeply grateful for his leadership, his generosity, and the care he brought to everything he touched, and we will carry that forward with us.”

#4402. 10 Legendary Grenades and Ordnances You Should Have in Borderlands 4

Aden Carter is a Contributor at DualShockers who has been covering games professionally since 2020. He specializes in lists and guides, with a focus on RPGs, horror games, survival horror, Soulslikes, cozy/sim games, and action-adventure titles. Before joining DualShockers, Aden contributed to GameRant, XDA, Gamepur, I

There are various types of legendary items in Borderlands 4, and it goes without saying that they are some of the best items in the game. Because of this, you will want to fill your endgame build with legendary items galore.

The main items you will be using across your builds are weapons, shields, and grenades. Once you have some powerful legendary weapons and have acquired a shield, you will need to focus on getting either a strong grenade or a strong ordnance. For a primary weapon, consider the best legendary assault rifles.

There are numerous legendary grenades and ordnances in Borderlands 4, and several of them are must-have items at this point in the game to refine your build with.

There are some grenades that you have to be careful about where you throw them, and then there are grenades that many refer to as “throw and forget” grenades. This is because you don’t need to worry about where you throw them. Instead, you can toss it in a general direction and go.

The Swarm is a grenade you can forget about because it homes in on targets. Its ability, Swoosh, makes it spawn three homing grenades on impact, and those spawn additional homing grenades for a total of nine.

If you happen to get bonuses on this build that increase your grenade damage and explosion size, you will be living the dream. You can get the Swarm from Sidney Pointylegs in Hungering Plain.

If you are someone who wants to use ordnances, your options are somewhat limited, as there aren’t as many of them in the game, but they are quite powerful. One of the more powerful ones is the Disc Jockey.

This heavy launcher has the ability Bouncing Biscuits, which makes it so it launches energy discs that bounce off surfaces. Each time one of these discs bounces, the damage of the disc increases by 20%.

This is a weapon that is great in small rooms, as the bounces can rack up some serious damage on groups of enemies. You can get this weapon from Sidney Pointylegs in Hungering Plain.

It is interesting whenever a grenade doesn’t deal grenade damage and instead gets all its power from another source. In the case of the Barb’ara, it gets its damage from your skill damage buffs, making it perfect for those who are running skill builds.

This grenade has the ability Tentacles, which causes it to create a tentacle explosion on impact. The explosion created by this impact deals skill damage. These tentacles will spawn two additional grenades that create more tentacles, also dealing skill damage.

Since every Vault Hunter in the game can run a skill build, this is a great grenade to have whenever you decide to switch up your build. You can farm this grenade from Crazed Earl in the Vault of the Damned DLC.

There are plenty of weapons in Borderlands 4 that have been added in DLC. Which ones of them are the best?

Sometimes you just want to fire a rocket launcher and let it delete your problems. In this case, the problem is usually a group of enemies or a massive boss that is blocking your path. The Loiter Sploiter is designed to take care of these problems quickly, and is great if you have an ordnance-focused build and amp gear.

The Loiter Sploiter’s ability, Sploiter, makes it so this weapon fires high-damage rockets. These rockets then spawn additional rockets when they explode, causing massive amounts of damage.

If you are running gear with the amped ability, this will power up these rockets, making them capable of one-shotting bosses with ease. You can get this weapon Infamous Dave in the Murders & Acquisitions DLC.

There are some grenades in Borderlands 4 that don’t just explode. Instead, they have some quirky effects such as shooting lasers or a machine gun at enemies before they explode. Either way, you get an explosion.

The Alignment is one of those grenades, as it has the ability Coordinated, which makes it so the grenade seeks out an enemy when thrown, hovers above them, shoots them with a beam of elemental energy, and then divebombs them.

It is an interesting effect that makes that weapon great for dealing elemental status effects, and therefore, is good for those who want an elemental status effect build. You can obtain this grenade from the Warped & Weird Vault Card.

Speaking of the weird and quirky, the Heimdahl is perhaps the weirdest of the ordnance weapons in Borderlands 4. This is because the weapon shoots Dahl soldier heads that attack enemies. They are out for revenge, and will kill anyone in their way.

The ability of this weapon is called Rig. It fires soldier heads that fly around the battlefield, track down enemies, and vomit on them. This deals significant damage, and is a weapon that you can fire and forget since it tracks enemies.

This weapon is perfect for Vault Hunter builds where you don’t need to worry about ordnance ammo, as you can just keep firing it and clear out a room in no time. You can obtain this weapon from Captain Willis in The Maelstrom in the Vault of the Damned DLC.

There are plenty of legendary assault rifles in Borderlands 4, and we will show you how to get them all.

The Blockbuster grenade is one that will clear an area with ease, but you better make sure to stay out of the area or you will get killed. This grenade is designed to do one thing, which is to cause numerous explosions.

The ability of this grenade is called Got You Covered, and it does give you plenty of cover. This ability makes the grenade split into four grenades on impact. These grenades then spawn an additional two grenades. This sounds normal until you realize that these grenades all bounce in place, creating explosions as they do.

It will cover the field in explosions, and you just need to stay out of the way so you don’t get killed. You can get this grenade from Vile Lictor in Terminus Range.

The Firepot is similar to the Swarm grenade, but it focuses on dealing fire damage and it loves to stick grenades to enemies. Torgue returns with one of the finest grenades in Borderlands 4, and it packs a serious punch.

The ability of this grenade is called Spicy, and it makes the grenade spawn homing Torgue sticky grenades that attach to enemies. In total, nine grenades will spawn from this bad boy, and they will each explode after 13 seconds, igniting the enemies that are unfortunate enough to be hit by them.

It is another throw and forget style grenade that does an amazing job covering the field without you needing to focus too much on what you are doing. You can get this grenade from Leader Willem in Grindstone of the Worthy.

The Waterfall was one of my first legendary grenades in Borderlands 4, so it holds a special place in my heart, and it might be a bit weaker than some of the other weapons on this list. However, this doesn’t mean that it isn’t worth getting, as it packs a serious punch.

This grenade has the Waterfall ability, which makes it explode multiple times whenever it hits an enemy. Throw it in a group, and each enemy damaged by the grenade will cause another explosion, cascading the damage over the surrounding area.

It can wipe out groups of enemies easily, but it is noticeably not as effective as the Swarm. You can get this grenade by farming Bio-Bulkhead in the Dissected Plateau.

There are some grenades and ordnances that can clear out entire rooms, and then there are some that are focused on one thing, and that is killing bosses. The Draupner is basically a delete button for life’s problems, and it is amazing.

Return Wave is the name of the Draupner’s ability, and it makes the weapon fire out three saw blades in a horizontal pattern from the weapon. These saw blades return to you after two seconds or upon impact, effectively hitting enemies twice over.

This ordnance effectively diminishes the damage numbers of every other ordnance in the game, making it a must-have weapon. You can obtain it by running the Takedown at the Hadron Abyss.

There are plenty of legendary weapons in Borderlands 4, but these are the weapons that you should have at this point if you want a strong build.

#4401. Two genes, two harvests: Adapting barley for double cropping

Growing two crops in succession on the same land requires a tight schedule. In parts of central and eastern China, farmers sow barley in autumn and harvest it in late spring. It is then followed by a summer crop, such as rice. For this cropping sequence to succeed, the barley must mature in time. An early harvest also helps the crop avoid heat and rain toward the end of the growing season.

#4398. Love and Deepspace 5.0 update brings together all five love interests for the first time

Love and Deepspace is getting a big update to celebrate its second anniversary, and there's a lot to dig through.

If you can believe it, Love and Deepspace is almost two-years-old, and Infold Games is celebrating the moment in a few major ways. The Throne of Eros update brings the game up to version 5.0, and it’s one for fans of all love interests.

For one, this is the first time all five of them are brought together. The update is also adding some important new features, alongside anniversary events, and more.

Throne of Eros also doubles as the new Wish Pool, which is the one that has all of the game’s love interests in a single banner. This is a limited-time affair, of course, but it’s not the only thing you should look forward to here.

There’s also the Memory Growth Bonus, another limited-time event that you can take advantage of to grow your Memories. The even bigger news is that you can target your Wishes through the Xspace Echo, which lets you select five Memories to create your own pool from. You can use this to get any Memories you might not have, of course.

On the topic of Memories, you’ll also be able to unlock new second anniversary KV Memories, as part of a Yearly Highlights Event that will let you look back on your own journey with the game over the past year.

On the story and narrative side, Throne of Eros adds two new main stories, with new branches for Xavier, and Rafayel. There’s even a narrative-specific event that will run throughout the anniversary period, through which you can earn two daily outfits for each of the five love interests.

The celebrations also extend to new anniversary content like mail, and video calls. You can purchase a Yearly Pass, and check out some new arrivals at the Lunar Shop.

Beyond the anniversary content, version 5.0 also adds a new feature to the game: Home, which essentially offers a hub to get you directly to interacting with love interests that doesn’t have to do with combat or story.

You can also expect various other quality of life updates that touch on the Journal, Phone Moments Search, Resources Quick Cleanup, and new Tete-a-Tete that should make interacting with all of them more streamlined.

While this is a special banner, you should brush up on how banners work in Love and Deepspace if you’re unfamiliar. As always, it’s never not a good idea to check our Love and Deepspace codes page for some freebies.

#4397. Track Attack: We Drive the 2028 Audi Nuvolari to the Limit

Unfamiliar surroundings can elicit feelings of uneasiness. We’re in Madrid; we’ve just rolled out of bed and arrived at Circuito de Madrid Jarama. A few minutes pass, and we’re belted into the passenger seat of the Audi’s newest halo car, the Audi Nuvolari, itself a relatively unexplored place. Site laps are sometimes easy, but not today. Our tour guide, Victor, has a crazy look in his eye. And maybe a screw loose. He attacks the braking zones, exits corners sideways, and shows zero restraint in his speed. Victor, we love you, but can you save a little tire for the rest of us?

We enjoyed our first experience with Audi’s first mid-engine car since the dearly departed R8. After just three laps driving around the former home of the Spanish Grand Prix, we love the Nuvolari. Having spent time with the Nuvolari’s donor plug-in hybrid platform, the Lamborghini Temerario, eases the tension.

The Audi’s cabin, a cocoon of microfiber and leather with aluminum door handles, seat controls, and vents, oozes fancy-dinner vibes more so than qualifying laps. It’s a welcoming environment. Strapped into the driver’s seat, the Nuvolari starts up in its pure electric mode. Turning the top-left knob on the busy steering wheel wakes the 789-hp twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8; its flat-plane crankshaft is capable of spinning to a bonkers 10,000 rpm. The cabin fills with glorious noise, most of it real. Turning and holding that same knob activates Dynamic+ mode, summons more noise, and puts most of the systems in their most-ready state.

See all results for new 2028 Audi Nuvolari for sale near 20147

Exiting Jarama’s final corner and pointing down the straight, the Nuvolari accelerates as if it were shot off an aircraft carrier’s flight deck. As in the Temerario, the screaming V-8 has friends. A 147-hp motor connected to the crankshaft fills the lulls in the engine’s torque delivery. The front axle has two 147-hp motors that also provide torque vectoring. While the Temerario stores its energy in a 4-kWh battery, the Nuvolari (like the new Lamborghini Revuelto SV) utilizes a larger 7-kWh pack. The new pack supplies up to 254 horses, compared to the Temerario’s 187-hp limit. In all, the V-8 and electric motors work together to create a 987-hp party, or 80 more than the Temerario.

By the end of Jarama’s nearly half-mile front straight, we’ve almost reached an indicated 185 mph. The Nuvolari brakes as effortlessly as it accelerates, courtesy of Brembo CCM-R Plus carbon-ceramic rotors (16.5-inch up front and 16.1-inch at the rear) that bite hard. The pedal doesn’t feel as wooden as the Lambo’s, where more force yields more stopping power. In the Nuvolari, a spring change within the brake actuator feels like it prioritizes pedal travel to modulate the brakes rather than pressure. Nevertheless, the pedal feels great.

See all results for new 2028 Audi Nuvolari for sale near 20147

Bending the Nuvolari into Turn 2 reveals off-center steering feel that isn’t nearly as over-caffeinated as the Lamborghini’s. Here, it feels very Audi. Effort ramps up in a linear fashion but is never too heavy. It’s as direct as it needs to be, and there’s ample indication when the front tires have had enough.

A nearly 1000-hp supercar should be somewhat intimidating to drive, but Audi has tuned the Nuvolari to be a gentle beast. Audi’s Quattro Predictive Drive system uses a 6-D sensor (as in the Revuelto SV) to absorb information from the car, and, based on driving habits, in-house-developed algorithms predict what the car should do next. Tail out on corner exit? The car’s computer brain might send a little extra torque vectoring to the front axle to keep things in check. Crank a little too much steering input into a large braking event? You can feel the motors straighten out the car.

The Predictive Drive system also communicates with the dampers. They’re adaptive units with high- and low-speed electronic controls for the compression and rebound sides. The dampers allow Audi to use a softer spring than the Temerario to help maintain a consistent tire patch and keep the car stable during braking and the body flat when the Bridgestone Potenza Race tires are loaded up midcorner.

With Predictive Drive working in the background, the rest of our extremely limited time in the Nuvolari is spent trying to digest the experience. Don’t forget to tug the massive aluminum shift paddles before slamming into the 10,000-rpm limiter. Check. What’s after this corner? I can’t remember; Victor said something about braking. Speaking of braking, is the rear motor really braking the engine when there’s more horsepower than is available for traction to harvest extra energy for the front straight? There’s no indication it’s happening, but we’ll take their word for it.

Familiarizing yourself with your very own Nuvolari will cost north of $700,000. That’s before customizing one of the 499 Nuvolaris that will be built. You can specify any color you’d like or choose an unpainted carbon-fiber body for an unspecified cost, something we’re excited to see. We’re even more excited to see how Audi’s return to the supercar world trickles down into the RS brand. We’ll be waiting.

#4396. Genshin Impact Version Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, including the long-awaited Moon Maiden Columbina

The first major Genshin Impact update in 2026 is almost here, bringing characters we've been waiting a while to play, and more besides.

Genshin Impact’s latest Special Program has spilled all the beans on the game’s next major update, Luna 4. The update, which arrives on January 14, kicks off 2026 with several bits of new content, including some previously-teased characters.

Dubbed Traveler on a Winter's Night, Luna 4 introduces three new playable characters, and brings back The Lantern Rite event to celebrate the beginning of the new year.

The first new arrival in Version Luna 4 is Columbina Hyposelenia, the Moon Maiden. Columbina is a 5-Star Hydro Catalyst wielder. Her kit revolves around supporting the squad via Lunar Reactions. She can trigger coordinated Lunar Reaction DMG, even when she’s off the field.

The Moon Maiden’s special ability, Lunar Domain, further boosts all Lunar Reactions by applying a DMG bonus, including summoning more thundercloud strikes for Lunar-Charged reactions. Columbina is also capable of converting Electro-Charged, Bloom, and Hydro Crystallize reactions into Lunar Reactions, as well as revive fallen squad members.

Speaking of elemental reactions, new in this version is Lunar-Crystallize, a new reaction that’s triggered when Geo meets Hydro (under certain conditions). When triggered, Lunar-Crystallize summons three Moondrifts near enemies. When triggered three times, Moondrift Harmony gets activated, dealing Geo DMG to enemies caught in its radius.

Then there’s Zibai, an Adeptus from Liyue. Zibai is another 5-Star character, a Geo Sword wielder. Zibai can, through entering a special state where they can build up energy, unleash an Elemental Skill that deals Lunar-Crystallize DMG.

The longer the fight goes on, the more Lunar-Crystallize reactions are triggered, the higher (and more often) the damage of Zibai’s Elemental Skill becomes.

Luna 4 continues the Nod-Krai story arc, with a big confrontation with Il Dottore. This is the focus of the new Archon Quest, completing which will earn you a new outfit. There’s a gameplay element to that new chapter, too, with the reveal of Piramida, a new area north of the region. Piramida is the headquarters of the Lightkeepers.

The first phase of Luna 4’s Event Wishes will, unsurprisingly, feature Columbina. It’ll also include reruns of Ineffa. The second phase is when Zibai becomes available, alongside another newcomer: Illuga, a 4-Star, polearm-wielding Geo Lightkeeper. The second phase’s rerun will be Neuvillette, who’s also going to have a new outfit in the shop at a discount.

Version Luna 4 brings back the annual Lantern Rite event, taking place in the mainland of Liyue. The event features its own set of minigames with unique rewards, alongside new stories of the Adepti.

All around Liyue Harbor, you’ll be able to place Xiao Lanterns and inscribe them with messages for others to read. You’ll also earn some Fortune Coins from Auspicious Treasure Trees, which you can later exchange for gifts.

All players will receive 1,600 Primogems through the in-game mail. If you log in regularly, you can earn up to ten Intertwined Fates. Lantern Rite has a new outfit for Yaoyao, which is also where you have a chance to earn one 4-Star Liyue character for free.

Finally, you can look forward to the new Classic Mode in Miliastra Wonderland, which lets you invite select Teyvat characters to join you.

#4394. Heartopia captures the hearts of Animal Crossing and The Sims fans to become the No.1 free download across 50 countries

Heartopia is officially the first big mobile launch of 2026, as the game grabs the attention of millions worldwide.

Heartopia, the new cosy life sim from XD Games, has officially arrived on mobile, right on schedule. If you’ve been keeping up with Heartopia news, you’re likely already aware that the game has pushed back its Steam release to an indeterminate point in 2026.

Doesn’t look like it mattered much, however, as this has already been a big launch on iOS and Android — it probably helps that PC players aren't being entirely left out of the fun, since the game is already available there via XD's own cross-device platform TapTap.

XD Games announced today that Heartopia has reached the top spot on the App Store’s downloads page for free games, and it managed to do so in more than 50 countries and regions worldwide.

The developer is celebratig by offering players a lot of free stuff. If you're feeling lucky, you’ll find new outfits and furniture in three gacha banners (Gilded Acorn Exhibitions): Polar Hymn, The Frostguard, and Coolplayism.

XD Games says you can expect regular updates to add more content, through Fashionwaves and Festivals. In fact, the first season - Winter Frost - is already penciled in for sometime in late January, and it’s going to add appropriately wintery activities like ice skating and snowman-building.

In February, a My Little Pony collaboration event will kick off, bringing new inspired outfits, and vehicles to the game.

Heartopia is a clever mix of Animal Crossing, and The Sims. It’s a free-to-play life sim where you can create your own character, dress them up, build a home for them (and decorate it), and go about town visiting and playing with other players’ characters.

The game’s main feature is the ability to take on a hobby, and seven of those are available at launch. You can dig deep into each hobby, either alone or with others, and there’s a progression track dedicated to each one.

Whether you’re among the millions who downloaded the game already, or you intend to so soon, we’ve got a set of helpful guides to get you started. #4392. Diablo 4's long-awaited Tower and its Leaderboards enter beta today, and there's no PTR funny business this time

Diablo 4's first big moment of 2026 is nearly upon us, and it's one feature many have been looking forward to for actual years.

Diablo 4 is about to deliver on Blizzard’s years-old promise to add a challenging, leaderboard-driven experience to the action RPG. The beta for The Tower, and its associated Leaderboards are about to kick off.

As recently revealed, the new experience launches today at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 7pm GMT. This is a beta version that arrives alongside update 2.5.2.

This early launch won’t offer the full experience, and it’s mainly designed to get it into the hands of players early so that Blizzard could get as much feedback as possible and incorporate it into the final version.

The beta is available to everyone, which is a nice change from the usual rigmarole players would have to go through to get the PTR build and play on a different branch. The Tower, and Leaderboards will be available only in the Seasonal Realm, however. Indeed, the plan is to build on what’s there with each future season, so it’s best to think of it as a seasonal experience.

The Tower is about as simple of an activity as you can get in an action RPG. The goal is to climb as many floors as you can as quickly as you can, all while battling increasingly difficult mobs.

You need to reach and beat the Tower’s final boss before you can call it a run. The Leaderboard will then show your time, and let you see how well you did compared to other players.

The Tower is available to anyone who completed Rank 2 of the current Season Rank. Once done, an Obelisk will appear in Cerrigar, letting you access the challenge.

The Leaderboards themselves will operate on a two-week schedule, all of which will take place during a given season. In this case, they’re going to close the day before Season of the Divine Interversion - the game’s current season - ends.

Blizzard published an updated set of patch notes that show how much has changed since The Tower, and Leaderboards first became playable in the patch 2.5.0 PTR.

Though the two new additions have been anticipated for a while, there’s not been much exciting going on in the world of Diablo 4, apart, of course, from the surprise arrival of The Paladin class, which became available in December last year to coincide with the announcement of Lord of Hatred, the game’s next expansion.
